entryAnswer.explanation:
What the code does. `spendingAlertsFor(graph, defaults)` binds one immutable defaults object and returns a `compose` function; configuration itself allocates no graph nodes (causal-entry.ts:48-51, README.md:82-84). Each `compose(inputs, overrides)` call invokes the existing complete host construction with that call's own inputs and resource (causal-entry.ts:52-69), so the two calls produce two independent running instances in the same Graph. Overrides only select `name`/`diagnostics` (causal-entry.ts:36-45, README.md:84-85). The second call passes `diagnostics: "summary"`, which adds the `${name}/diagnosticSummary` node (causal-preset.ts:70, 180-190); the first keeps the default `"off"`. Each instance's own `.view` is passed to `mountSpendingView` with its own render callback; the returned function ends observation only (causal-view-binding.ts:16-20, 32-36).

What the application must retain after either display is unmounted. Detaching a panel stops observation; the running instance keeps its outstanding obligations (README.md:143). The application must keep, per instance: the owning Graph and the original composed instance together (README.md:100-104); the original `owner` and `inspect` diagnostics (causal-graded-demo.ts:65, 140-143, 185-188); the original view and capability references, including the retained lineage (`app.capabilities.retained.execution === execution`, causal-graded-demo.ts:85-87, 283-287); and the host's retained request/admission/outcome records, which are bounded at 64 distinct records per owned epoch plus one in-flight write (causal-focused-host.ts:140, 368-373, 571-575; README.md:146-151). Panel cleanup is not recovery: an unknown or reconcile-required outcome is not success and prevents normal-end readiness (causal-focused-host.ts:224, 517-535, 563-564; README.md:149-151). The demo's final forced cleanup is test cleanup, not normal lifecycle completion (causal-graded-demo.ts:312-320; README.md:156-157).

What the distinct names contribute. Names are the per-instance node-name prefix: `spendingNodeNames(name, diagnostics)` builds `${name}/startup`, `${name}/...`, `${name}/causal/...`, `${name}/publication` (causal-preset.ts:60-72), and the host adds `${name}/hostFacts`, `${name}/hostGuard`, `${name}/runEndReady`, `${name}/hostPackFacts` (causal-focused-host.ts:81-87). Distinct names keep the two instances' nodes and edges distinguishable in one shared Graph, so inspection can select the intended instance rather than the first node ending in `/causal/authority` (README.md:118-120). A name is not an authorization token: changing `name` does not clone input Nodes, create an independent resource or rewrite its binding (README.md:85-89).

What the independently prepared input Nodes contribute. Each `SpendingCreationInputs` carries its own `evaluations` (pack, arrivals, current), `verification.receipts`, `localAuthority.facts` and `inbox.resource` (causal-entry.ts:15-17; causal-inputs.ts:106-115). The host requires six distinct input nodes and rejects duplicates (causal-preset.ts:73-93), and it validates each frame against the resource's binding (causal-inputs.ts:352-377). So the two inputs are separate evidence/permission lanes: separate evaluation packs, receipts, grants and current facts, each bound to its own `SpendingBinding` (causal-inputs.ts:14-17, 212-224).

What the resource bindings contribute. `compose` requires a prepared `SpendingResource` and passes `resource.binding` and the resource itself to the host (causal-entry.ts:55-68). The host validates the binding and requires `same(resource.binding, binding)` (causal-focused-host.ts:74-77), then claims the resource for that epoch (causal-focused-host.ts:96, 110; causal-resource.ts:69-99). A resource can be claimed once per epoch (causal-resource.ts:70-72), so each instance needs its own prepared resource with its own binding; the binding's `compositionEpoch`/`hostEpoch`/`destinationRef`/digests are what the host checks against each request (causal-focused-host.ts:344-359, 388-397). Changing a name does not prepare or rebind a resource; the two supplied inputs and resources are preserved as given.

Scope note: the snippet only composes and mounts; it does not open resources, invent input facts, or invoke a transport directly. Normal host behavior (including the offline simulated writer) is allowed and not disabled. The snippet was not executed.
